claim: For EVERY rank2 orthogonal projector P with P/2 separable, and EVERY arbitrary complex traceless original 4×4 A,B, Tr[P(A⊗I+I⊗B)†(A⊗I+I⊗B)]≤2(||A||F²+||B||F²). This pays non-CC projectors with positive real variance form, not merely the previously paid product-basis-diagonal/singular-K boundary. The remaining full original T2 test-projector domain is ENTIRELY ENTANGLED P/2; no claim about that domain or outside-f274 pairs.
projector_classification: Every separable rank2 projector has an orthonormal product basis. If its 2D support is a common-local-factor subspace, this is immediate. Otherwise two spanning product vectors have both local factors independent, so their span has exactly two product rays; a separable decomposition uses only these rays, and their positive weighted rank-one sum equals the identity on the 2D support only if the normalized two vectors are orthogonal with weights one. Orthogonality of product vectors means at least one local pair is orthogonal.
nonorthogonal_second_factor_proof: Take P=|1,b⟩⟨1,b|+|2,d⟩⟨2,d|, ⟨1,2⟩=0, r=|⟨b,d⟩|<1. For A diagonals z1,z2 and s=z1+z2, q=z1−z2, tracezero gives its gap ≥|q|²/2+3|s|²/2. Put S=|b⟩⟨b|+|d⟩⟨d|, W=2I−S>0, C=z1|b⟩⟨b|+z2|d⟩⟨d|. The B gap is ||BW^(1/2)||F²−2Re⟨C,B⟩, and TrB=0 allows subtraction of λI. Exact minimization yields min_λ||(C−λI)W^(−1/2)||F²=|q|²/2+[(1+5r²)/(2(3−r²))]|s|². Difference from the A lower bound is 4(1−r²)/(3−r²)|s|²≥0. r=1 is a product projector, paid directly.
